component.name: BakeFix
component.description: Question answering over the user's own kitchen documents (recipes, baking notes, appliance manuals), with sources, traces, and a Kestrel sample knowledge base.

properties.name: bakefix:scope
properties.value: Bundled models, datasets, services, and pinned packages. Documents uploaded at runtime are not included.

components.name: all-MiniLM-L6-v2
components.description: Turns passages and questions into 384-dimensional vectors for dense (semantic) search. Runs locally; no text leaves the machine.

modelParameters.modelArchitecture: BertModel, 6 layers, hidden size 384, mean pooling

inputs.format: English text, truncated at 256 word pieces

outputs.format: 384-dimensional embedding vector, compared by cosine distance

datasets.name: Sentence pairs used to fine-tune all-MiniLM-L6-v2
datasets.description: Over 1 billion sentence pairs (Reddit comments 2015-2018, S2ORC, WikiAnswers, Stack Exchange, MS MARCO, and others) with a contrastive objective, per the model's published card. Not inspected by us.

performanceMetrics.slice: Baking corpus, 10 answerable questions, dense only, chunks 800/80 (evaluation/results/v3/baking_dense_800_80_summary.jsonl)
Kestrel KB, 8 answerable questions, dense only, chunks 800/80 (evaluation/results/v3/kestrel_dense_800_80_summary.jsonl)

graphics.description: No graphics. Small evaluation sets (8 to 10 questions): one question changes hit rate by 0.10 to 0.125, so these are indications, not precise scores.

users: Home cooks using BakeFix on their own computer
useCases: Ranking document passages by meaning for a question, fused with BM25 keyword search
technicalLimitations: Trained mainly on English web text (Reddit, Stack Exchange, and other sentence pairs, over 1 billion in total, per the model's own card); other languages retrieve poorly.
Text after 256 word pieces is ignored, so the end of an 800-character passage can be missed.
Weak on exact identifiers such as error codes (KST-5031); BM25 is used alongside it for that reason.

ethicalConsiderations.name: Training data may carry biases from web text
ethicalConsiderations.mitigationStrategy: Used only to rank passages; every answer cites the passages it used, so a poor ranking is visible.

performanceTradeoffs: Small (about 22 million parameters, 6 layers) so it embeds on a laptop CPU in milliseconds, at lower accuracy than larger embedding models.
The right passage is in the top 5 far more often than at rank 1, so BakeFix gives the model several passages instead of one.

fairnessAssessments.groupAtRisk: People who write questions or documents in languages other than English
fairnessAssessments.benefits: Fast, private search for English kitchen documents
fairnessAssessments.harms: Poorer retrieval, so more 'not in your documents' answers
fairnessAssessments.mitigationStrategy: BM25 keyword search runs alongside it; the limitation is stated in the README and report.

properties.name: bakefix:energy
properties.value: Runs locally on CPU; re-embedding the bundled corpus (68 baking chunks) takes seconds. No GPU or data-centre use.

components.name: en_core_web_sm
components.description: spaCy English pipeline used by Microsoft Presidio to find personal data (names, places) in the question before it is sent to Gemini. Runs locally.

modelParameters.modelArchitecture: spaCy small English pipeline with named-entity recognition

outputs.format: Entity spans (PERSON, LOCATION, ...) that Presidio replaces with placeholders

datasets.name: spaCy en_core_web_sm training data
datasets.description: OntoNotes 5, ClearNLP Constituent-to-Dependency Conversion, and WordNet 3.0, per the model's meta.json. Not inspected by us.

useCases: Redacting personal data from questions before they leave the machine
technicalLimitations: Small model: misses some names and tags some product names as people (e.g. 'Vellora' was tagged PERSON in V4 testing). For this reason it runs on the question only; document passages get email and phone patterns only.

ethicalConsiderations.name: Personal data that is not detected is sent to Google
ethicalConsiderations.mitigationStrategy: Documented as an accepted risk; users are told not to upload documents they would not share with Google.

performanceTradeoffs: Small and fast (runs on every question in milliseconds) at the cost of missed and false entities; the large spaCy model would catch more but needs about 500 MB.

fairnessAssessments.groupAtRisk: People whose names are uncommon in English news and web text
fairnessAssessments.benefits: Names that are detected are not sent to Google
fairnessAssessments.harms: Their names are detected less reliably, so they are more likely to reach Google unredacted
fairnessAssessments.mitigationStrategy: Questions rarely need names; documented as an accepted risk.

performanceMetrics.slice: Published by spaCy for OntoNotes 5 (meta.json of en_core_web_sm 3.8.0); not measured on BakeFix questions

graphics.description: News-style benchmark scores; product names in kitchen manuals (e.g. 'Vellora') are outside that domain, which is why redaction runs on the question only.

components.name: gemini-3.5-flash-lite
components.description: The hosted Gemini model that writes BakeFix's answers. Weights, training data, and version history are Google's and not visible to us; listed so its limits and our measurements are recorded next to the other models.

modelParameters.architectureFamily: transformer (not published in detail by Google)

inputs.format: Prompt with tagged retrieved passages, graph paths (Kestrel only), answer-style instructions, and the redacted question

outputs.format: JSON: status, answer, cited chunk IDs, glossary; rejected if invalid or if it cites passages that were not retrieved

performanceMetrics.slice: Baking, 10 answerable + 2 out-of-scope questions; both refusals correct (evaluation/results/baking_rag_reviewed.jsonl)
Kestrel, 10 questions; both wrong answers were 'not found' although the evidence had been retrieved (evaluation/results/kestrel_rag_reviewed.jsonl)

graphics.description: Measured before the V4 prompt framing and answer-style changes; small sets, so indications only.

useCases: Answering from the retrieved passages only, with citations
technicalLimitations: Can refuse when the answer is in the passages (both Kestrel errors), or state something the passages do not support; citations are checked to exist, not that they support each sentence.
Can follow instructions hidden in a document (prompt injection). Mitigated by the upload scanner, tagged passages, output validation, and safe rendering.
Google can change the model behind the same name; results are not reproducible over time.
performanceTradeoffs: The 'flash-lite' tier is cheap and fast (about 1.5 s per answer) at the cost of some over-refusal.

ethicalConsiderations.name: User data is processed by Google
ethicalConsiderations.mitigationStrategy: Personal data is redacted from the question and email/phone patterns from passages before sending; stated in the README.

ethicalConsiderations.name: Confident wrong answers in a cooking context (temperatures, food safety)
ethicalConsiderations.mitigationStrategy: Every answer shows its numbered sources and the passages behind them, so the reader can check; the answer is withheld if it cites a passage that was not retrieved.

services.name: LLM API (OpenAI-compatible; default Google Gemini)
services.description: Writes the answer, citations, and glossary from the retrieved passages, and extracts concept graphs. The server and model are chosen with LLM_URL, LLM_API_KEY and LLM_MODEL (any OpenAI-compatible API, including a local one); the default recorded here is Google Gemini. A provider may update the model behind a name.

data.description: The user's question after personal-data redaction (Presidio), the retrieved passages after email and phone redaction, and the answer-style settings.
Answer, cited chunk IDs, and glossary as JSON; validated before it is shown.

properties.name: bakefix:limits
properties.value: 30 s timeout, 1 retry, at most 4,096 output tokens per answer.

properties.name: bakefix:offline_use
properties.value: Built the Kestrel knowledge graph (kestrel-kb/graph/graph.json) from the Kestrel documents with backend/graph_extraction.py. graph.json does not record which model name was used.
